basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 5.' and it opens '(Cap. XXX.—Vers. 5 et 6.) Et concepit Bala, et peperit Jacob filium: et dixit Rachel:'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXX.—Vers. 5 et 6.) Et concepit Bala, et peperit Jacob filium: et dixit Rachel: Judicavit me Dominus, et exaudivit vocem meam, et dedit mihi filium: propterea vocavit nomen ejus Dan. Causam nominis expressit, ut ab eo quod judicasset se Dominus, filio ancillae, judicii nomen imponeret: DAN (דן) quippe interpretatur judicium.
